scope: pixels only: specified current full-cycle-07 beauty, neutral, UV-standard and approved spawn reference renders; no native/technical evidence reviewed

category_scores.name: Scale, layout and route readability
evidence: C01_ENTRY: centerline markings and scanner opening make the entry sequence easy to parse.
C02_HERO_DOCK and CORNER_SW/SE/NW/NE: the main route and functional zones are generally legible in the open cutaways.

C06_CART_GATE_G1: the foreground scanner post, movable screening panels and adjacent machine obscure the bypass clearance in this camera; this is a camera-occlusion/readability issue, not proof the physical route is blocked.
PLAYER_PINCH: a floor strip and trench are readable, but the relation between them and the usable path remains visually cramped.
category_scores.reason: The layout communicates a coherent entry-to-inspection route and has generous visible floor area. Circulation evidence loses clarity at the cart bypass and north return, while blank spans and few human-scale anchors weaken scale judgment.

category_scores.name: Grounded stylized shape language and object-specific construction
evidence: C01_ENTRY / HERO_SCANNER: the biometric arch has a clear manufactured silhouette, but its tall rectangular blue uprights, broad header and repeated box posts dominate as primitive masses.
C05_CONVEYOR_LEAD_TUNNEL / HERO_CARGO: the cargo tunnel and conveyor have useful functional structure, yet read mainly as large box frames, flat panels and repeated square supports.
CORNER_SW/SE/NW/NE: black structural uprights repeat as blunt rectangular bars with little visible attachment or section variation.
C03_CHECKIN_COUNTER / DETAIL_CHECKIN: the hatch, ledge and desk props add object-specific secondary forms, but most construction remains simplified to slabs and boxes.
category_scores.reason: Several hero props are recognizable and have purposeful framing, hinges, rollers and controls. Repeated rectangular masses and uniform support bars still produce a procedural, box-led read that falls short of the specified specific industrial construction.

category_scores.name: Inspection/check-in hero hierarchy and functional composition
evidence: C02_HERO_DOCK: the scanner is the dominant focal object; the check-in hatch is pushed to the extreme left and is partly cropped, so the two intended lead functions do not share the composition.
C04_SCANNER_APPROACH / HERO_SCANNER: arch opening, indicator lights and threshold plate read clearly, but the header text is small and the adjacent screening panels compete with the arch.
C03_CHECKIN_COUNTER / DETAIL_CHECKIN: papers, stamp, tray and communication grille communicate check-in work; the counter elevation and props are visually compressed into a shallow band.
C05_CONVEYOR_LEAD_TUNNEL / HERO_CARGO: cargo scanning is clearly staged, though machine, crate and sign compete for attention and the actual cargo path is difficult to read past the large crate.
category_scores.reason: The scanner and cargo tunnel have unmistakable focal hierarchy and the desk detail conveys check-in. The counter is secondary in the wide composition, while some equipment crowds its own functional presentation.

category_scores.name: Tactile material identity and UV/texture discipline
evidence: Beauty C05_CONVEYOR_LEAD_TUNNEL and neutral counterpart: painted metal, darker frame, pale crate and textile cover separate by broad color/value, but most surfaces remain smooth, flat and weakly differentiated at close range.

HERO_UTILITIES / neutral counterpart: blue cabinets, dark backing plate, light enclosures and metallic service pipes are distinct by color; roughness/finish differences are subtle and broad surfaces show little tactile variation.
UV-standard HERO_TROLLEY: checker pattern is broadly regular over the main draped face, with localized cell deformation around the curved canopy transitions and small attachments.

UV-standard HERO_UTILITIES: checker cells visibly elongate around narrow pipes, joints and curved/cylindrical service parts; distortion is localized to those forms. Checker discontinuities at panel seams and changed checker phase are not counted as stretch.
UV-standard C05_CONVEYOR_LEAD_TUNNEL: cells remain generally legible on major machine panels; narrow rollers/rails and small hardware show pronounced compression/stretch.
category_scores.reason: The neutral images confirm recognizable broad material families, but the beauty render does not give them strong tactile separation. UV checks reveal localized stretching on curved fabric and narrow service geometry; there is no basis to call every seam or phase shift a UV defect.

category_scores.name: Localized lighting, depth and bleak atmosphere without hiding geometry
evidence: C01_ENTRY / C04_SCANNER_APPROACH: the arch is locally highlighted and its lights provide a useful focal accent.
C02_HERO_DOCK / C07_OFFICE_INTERIOR: large dark ceiling and office shadows lose structural detail; the glazing also reads dark and reflective rather than clearly separating room layers.
CORNER cutaways and WALL elevations: practical pools create depth, but long blush wall expanses are evenly lit and visually empty while corners and support spaces fall very dark.
C08_CONCEALED_SUPPORT_H1 / HERO_EVIDENCE: the trolley and cabinets are lit enough to read, with black support posts and deep recesses merging into the background.
category_scores.reason: Warm practicals and deep shadows support a bleak institutional mood and generally preserve hero readability. The balance is inconsistent: dark areas conceal detail and large lit wall areas remain flat, with limited separation between primary and secondary pools.

category_scores.name: Approved spawn colour coherence and restrained accents
evidence: VALIDATE_Spawn / BRIEFING_INDIRECT: approved reference uses dusty pink and deep blue/charcoal masses with orange-red accents.
C01_ENTRY / CORNER views: the dock repeats dusty pink walls, deep blue/charcoal structures and restrained terracotta/orange signage and floor marks.
C02_HERO_DOCK / C09_ARRIVAL_GATE_P2: the orange-red signs and floor safety markings are coherent with the spawn palette, though the dock is more subdued and less warm overall.
category_scores.reason: The principal color families clearly align with the approved spawn palette and accents mostly serve route/function. Coherence is strong; variation in warmth is an intentional mood shift rather than a mismatch.

category_scores.name: Purposeful worker traces and coercive institutional storytelling
evidence: WALL_OFFICE_FRONT / C02_HERO_DOCK: “WE VALUE YOUR TIME” and “ALL DELAYS ARE YOUR RESPONSIBILITY” are legible and make the reassuring branding coercive on closer read.
HERO_CARGO: custody marking and orange hazard signage connect the machinery to inspection and evidence handling.
HERO_EVIDENCE: sealed cabinets and a posted “DO NOT RELEASE” paper imply controlled evidence storage.

C03_CHECKIN_COUNTER / DETAIL_CHECKIN / C07_OFFICE_INTERIOR: paperwork and office equipment provide function, but the space has almost no personal possessions, work interruption, repair history or accumulated human traces.
WALL_SOUTH / WALL_EAST / WALL_WEST and cutaways: broad empty wall fields and uncluttered floors leave the institution visually generic outside the main equipment clusters.
category_scores.reason: The signage establishes a clear coercive institutional subtext and evidence handling is legible. The human story is thin: a few forms and sparse surface wear do not show sustained worker presence, repair pressure or lived-in history.

defects.region: C02 left foreground and right inspection cluster; C06 central/right bypass aperture; PLAYER_PINCH center-left threshold
defects.finding: The wide composition gives the scanner the whole focal hierarchy while cutting the check-in area off at frame-left. In the bypass view, adjacent posts/panels and the inspection machine obscure the apparent usable gap. This is a readability/occlusion finding only; the pixels do not establish a blocked route.

defects.region: Scanner uprights/header; tunnel frame and conveyor supports; repeated black room uprights
defects.finding: Repeated rectangular beams, posts and broad box panels dominate important silhouettes. The props remain identifiable, but the repeated box-and-bar construction weakens object-specific authored form.

defects.region: Curved canopy transitions, narrow pipes/joints and roller/rail hardware
defects.finding: The checker shows local deformation on curves and thin parts. Main panels remain mostly legible. Checker seams and phase discontinuities are not treated as evidence of stretch by themselves. The neutral/beauty comparisons show limited tactile response between several large painted surfaces.

defects.region: Ceiling beams, office glazing, deep equipment recesses and support-space corners
defects.finding: Crushed dark values conceal secondary construction and glazing reads as a dark reflective slab. Bright wall pools are broad and even, reducing lighting hierarchy across those areas.

defects.region: Office/counter wall, evidence storage and blank perimeter wall fields
defects.finding: The coercive slogans and custody label are clear, but there is little accumulated worker presence, repair history or lived-in detail. Large empty wall and floor areas dilute the otherwise specific institutional story.

gate_assessment: FAIL visual score threshold: the seven visual category mean and individual scores do not meet the owner requirement of overall >=99 / every category >93. No critical visual defect ID is asserted from the permitted pixels alone. This is not runtime approval.
